_meta.why_a_separate_file: docs/mesh_rev1/matrice4e_acceptance_thresholds.json was frozen before the first acceptance run and is NOT edited; its sha256 is still 58872e31193330861cc3220277fabf91046c9aef3df5872566b1afddf0333942 and still matches the registry. Deviations found AFTER that run are recorded here, dated, each with the reason and with the original row kept in the table as report-only so that nothing disappears (plan C threshold freeze, critique M8).
_meta.rule: A deviation may only REPLACE a row that cannot be reached by the model this revision is (an exterior-only surface model) or that asks for a physically impossible number. It may never widen a tolerance on a quantity the model can actually hit. Each entry says what is scored instead and why that is testable.
_meta.source_of_the_defects: scratch/wf/b2_matrice4e_verify.md (adversarial review 2026-09-18), defects D9 and the C.5 az180 row
_meta.why_the_rename: RULING 4 (main session, 2026-09-18): deviations that live in code must move into a file, and every drone's post-run deviations must be found under one name so that the pre-deviation count is recoverable by moving one file aside. phantom4 already uses docs/mesh_rev1/phantom4_acceptance_deviations.json; matrice4e now uses the same name. The frozen threshold file is still untouched and its sha256 still matches the registry.

rulings_applied.1: Interior surfaces of a CAD reference cannot be matched by an exterior-only mesh. Such a row stays in the table with its measured value as a report row, its visible fraction is printed next to it, and a NARROWED row measured on the visible part of the same CAD class is added and scored. The failing number never disappears.
rulings_applied.2: A threshold is never relaxed to make a row pass. Where a bound is unmeetable by construction the MEASUREMENT is fixed (DEV-8 C.7, DEV-9 C.2c) and the corrected measurement is scored, whether it passes or fails.
rulings_applied.4: Deviations live in this file, not in the scoring code.

_meta.visibility_measurement: scratch/mesh_rev1/b4/matrice4e/work/cad_face_visibility.py — the whole CAD z-buffer rendered from 200 aspects (13 elevations x 18 azimuths, poles once) at 1100 px over a 270 mm half-extent; a triangle counts as visible when it shows at least one pixel in at least one view. Cached as cad_face_visible.npz next to cad_tris.npz and read by mesh_rev1_acceptance_matrice4e.cad_visible_mask.

deviations.from: C4_reference_distance.cad_classes.nose_cradle = [56, 57, 58, 49], scored at median <= 5.0 mm and p90 <= 8.6 mm (plan B.3 row M4E-2)
deviations.to: the SCORED class nose_cradle is CAD solid 49 only (the exterior gimbal cradle). Solids 56, 57 and 58 become a new report-only class `nose_interior`, whose distances are printed for both revisions but not scored.
deviations.reason: Solids 56, 57 and 58 are nose structure that sits inside the shell; solid 49 is the exterior gimbal cradle. Measured here, not assumed (fix_0918/cad_visibility.py): the whole CAD was z-buffer rendered from 200 aspects (azimuth every 20 deg at elevations -75..+75 deg every 15 deg, plus nadir and zenith) and the share of each solid's own triangles that is visible was counted per view. Solid 49 shows 17.0 % of its triangles per view and the six shell solids 13.3-28.8 %; solids 56, 57 and 58 show 1.8 %, 2.8 % and 5.8 %. ⚠ CORRECTION, 2026-09-18: an earlier draft of this entry said they are NEVER visible. That is wrong and the measurement above is what replaced it — a little of each does show, through the gimbal aperture and the open nose. What the measurement does support is that they are overwhelmingly interior: the CAD->ours distance on them is median 12.06 mm and p90 19.43 mm for revision 1 and 16.68 / 24.27 mm for revision 0, i.e. no exterior-only surface model, before or after this revision, is anywhere near them, so the row scores the absence of interior structure rather than the quality of the exterior fit. The threshold file's own C.4 preamble says the comparison is against 'our exterior surface'. Scored on solid 49 alone, revision 1 is at median 1.01 / p90 6.15 mm, inside the frozen 5.0 / 8.6 limits, and revision 0 is at 2.11 / 10.04, outside them.
deviations.evidence_limits: A z-buffer visibility share is not a proof of interiority; it is the strongest test this unit could run on the triangulated STEP. The independent review reached the same split by a different route (inside/outside against the shell's local half width). If the user wants this settled harder, the test is a solid containment check against a closed union of the CAD's exterior solids, which needs a watertight CAD union this unit does not have.

deviations.from: C5_facing.hard.metal_facing10_az180_el0_mm2_max = 0.0, where metal = the battery and motor groups (drones.DRONE_GROUP_MAT)
deviations.to: two scored rows — (i) metal facing az180 el0 (10 deg) from every metal group EXCEPT the motor cans must be 0, and (ii) the motor-can contribution is scored against the CAD's own motor solids at the same aspect and cone, as a ratio inside the band the threshold file already uses for its other CAD-ratio rows. The original all-metal row is kept as report-only.
deviations.reason: The target as written is unreachable with metal motors present, and revision 1 did not put the metal there: the row's own note says revision 0's 3,288 mm2 is the battery's rear face, and M4E-3 removed exactly that (battery metal at az 180 is now 0). What is left is the four motor cans, 603 mm2, and the CAD shows straight-walled metal cans in the same place. Asking for 0 asks the model to hide metal the aircraft has. The restated rows test what is testable: that the tail closes over the pack (the change M4E-3 actually made), and that the cans do not present more metal than the CAD's cans do.
scored_instead: C.5 facing/non-motor metal facing az180 el0 (10 deg)
C.5 facing/motor metal facing az180 el0 (10 deg) ratio to CAD motor solids
kept_as_report: C.5 facing/metal facing az180 el0 (10 deg), all metal groups (frozen row)
deviations.tolerance_note: The new ratio row uses the band [0.3, 2.1] that the frozen file already states for the az180 facing5 CAD-ratio row, applied to the same aspect. No number is invented for it, and it is stricter than 'report only'.
deviations.pre_registration_note: The motor cans also raise nose-on metal from 91 to about 444 mm2 at az 0 el 0. Neither that nor the az 180 603 mm2 is in the plan's pre-registered list of census-predicted changes (plastic-nose band, az 180 battery window, near-nadir plate). Both must be added to outputs/mesh_rev1_prereg.json before any RF run, or they will read as breaks.

deviations.from: C4_reference_distance — plan C.4 'no worse than revision 0 in any region', scored on the p99 of the nearest-surface distance of a whole CAD class
deviations.to: for the four rows listed below the p99 row becomes REPORT-ONLY with its measured value printed, and a narrowed row 'p99 (visible surface only)' is scored in its place, measured on the part of the same CAD class that is externally visible; the visible fraction is printed as its own row
deviations.reason: These four rows fail on the reference's INTERIOR structure, which an exterior-only surface model has nothing to be near. Measured, not assumed, by the 200-aspect z-buffer visibility above: the front motor bell 105 shows 51.4 % of its triangles and the prop mount 103 71.6 %, but the bell's inner wall belongs to the same solids and never shows; the RTK cap solids 26/122 show 46.4 % / 51.1 %; the gimbal cradle's exterior solid 49 shows 88.7 % against 44.3 / 41.8 / 52.8 % for the interior solids 56/57/58. The worst 1 % of each failing row was located per solid in the 2026-09-18 fix round: the motors row's worst 25 CAD points sit at z = 3.1-3.3 mm inside the bell's height band, i.e. on its inner surfaces, which a solid can cannot have; the turret rows' worst points sit at z 88.5-89.2 mm within r <= 14.1 mm of the turret axis, i.e. on the cap's inner face. Narrowing the measurement to the visible surface is a change of MEASUREMENT, not of tolerance: the same rev0 + 0.5 mm rule is applied to the narrowed row, with revision 0 re-measured on the same subset.

rows.why: the motor bell's inner wall: a closed 27.0 x 16.3 mm can has no inner surface
the gimbal cradle's interior, reached through the nose aperture
the RTK cap's inner face at z 88.5-89.2 mm, r <= 14.1 mm
our cap points whose nearest CAD triangle is the cap's inner face

deviations.evidence_limits: A z-buffer visibility share is a lower bound on what an exterior model can reach, not a proof of interiority; a triangle that shows one pixel in one of 200 aspects counts as visible, so the narrowing is conservative. A stricter test is solid containment against a watertight union of the CAD's exterior solids, which this unit does not have.

deviations.from: C7_props.blade_angle_max_abs_diff_deg_vs_rev0 = 0.2, scored on `angle_inertia_deg`, the first principal axis of a cylindrical section's surface samples
deviations.to: that row becomes REPORT-ONLY with its measured value; the SCORED rows are the constructed pitch law and the constructed chord law at the same r/R, and the mirror-consistent measured comparison (revision 1's mirrored propeller against revision 0's plain one) is printed next to it
deviations.reason: The bound is unmeetable by construction and the measurement, not the threshold, is what is wrong. What P6 changes IS the section the angle is measured on: drone_parts_rev1.blade_rev1 mirrors the chord coordinate (Polygon(-x, y), line 1337) so that the thick rounded edge leads, and flips the sign of the skimitar sweep (line 1341). A cambered section's principal axis is not invariant under a chordwise mirror, so the reading moves even though the pitch the builder applies has not changed at all. Both revisions reach the same laws through the same resolvers with the same arguments (drone_cad.build_propeller_cad line 3451 and drone_parts_rev1.propeller_rev1 line 1389 both pass root_frac=0.070; both resolve blade_law with geom.blade_law_canon() and the chord profile with drone_cad.resolve_chord_max_over_r / resolve_chord_profile), so theta(r) = atan(k(r/R) * P / (2 pi r)) and c(r) = interp(r/R, chord_rr, chord_frac) * c_max/R * R are the same functions for both. The acceptance now recomputes them and scores the difference with the frozen tolerances unchanged (0.2 deg and 0.5 mm).
scored_instead: C.7 propeller/constructed pitch law change r/R=...
C.7 propeller/constructed chord law change r/R=...
kept_as_report: C.7 propeller/blade angle change r/R=... (measured principal axis)
C.7 propeller/blade angle change r/R=..., mirror-consistent
deviations.evidence_limits: The constructed law is what the builder is instructed to build; it is not a measurement of the built mesh. It is paired here with the mirror-consistent measured comparison so that a reader sees both. If the user wants the built mesh scored instead, the sound measurement is the chord line taken between the two points of the section that the airfoil generator calls leading and trailing edge, which needs the generator to carry those labels into the mesh — it does not today.

deviations.from: C2_attachment.swept_disc_frame_clearance_mm_min = 1.0, measured on the mesh VERTICES of the propeller and of the frame, binned 2 mm in radius
deviations.to: that row becomes REPORT-ONLY with its measured value; the SCORED row is the same quantity measured on evenly sampled SURFACES of both bodies, and revision 0 and the CAD airframe are measured the same way and printed as controls
deviations.reason: The vertex reading has holes. Both bodies are lofts whose rings are tens of millimetres apart, so most 2 mm radial bins hold only the vertices of one ring: on revision 1's rotor 0 the vertex envelope reads 17.091 mm at r = 108-110 mm where the blade's surface reaches 13.894 mm, and the front arm carries no vertex at all between 121 and 171 mm from the rotor axis, which is exactly where the arm rises into the disc. The vertex reading of +1.006 mm is therefore not a 6 micrometre margin, it is a miss. The surface measurement is strictly more conservative and has no free parameter beyond the sample count, which is checked for stability.
scored_instead: C.2 attachment/frame clearance to the swept blade volume (surface sampled)
kept_as_report: C.2 attachment/frame clearance to the swept blade volume (mesh vertices)
C.2 attachment/CAD airframe clearance to our swept blade volume (control)
deviations.evidence_limits: The corrected row FAILS, and it fails for revision 0 as well and for the CAD airframe itself: see the two control rows. Nothing here rescues the row — it makes an already-broken row honest.

deviations.from: C5_facing.cad_ratio_rows.az180_el0_facing5.band = [0.3, 2.1], applied by DEV-6 to the motor group's facing area inside a 10 deg cone at az 180 el 0
deviations.to: that row becomes REPORT-ONLY with its measured value and its two unresolvable neighbours; the SCORED row is the same ratio inside a 45 deg cone, which our mesh resolves, and the cone-free visible-silhouette ratio is printed next to it
deviations.reason: The 10 deg cone is below the angular resolution of a 24-segment can, and the measurement says so itself. Our motor cans and prop adapters are 24-gons, so their facet normals are 15 deg apart: measured at az 180 el 0 on revision 1, the 5 deg cone returns exactly 0.0 mm2 (no facet normal lands inside it) while the 10 deg and the 20 deg cones return the SAME 603.1 mm2, because the two facets at +-7.5 deg are wholly inside both. A quantity that is 0 at 5 deg and identical at 10 and 20 deg is reading the facet pitch, not the shape. The CAD's finely tessellated bells behave like a smooth surface over the same cones: 92.9 / 213.4 / 525.7 mm2 at 5 / 10 / 20 deg, in the sin(theta) ratio a cylinder gives. Analytically, a 27.0 mm can plus adapter (23.81 mm of metal height) presents 111.6 mm2 per rotor inside a 10 deg cone if it is smooth and 83.9 or 166.4 mm2 as a 24-gon depending on which phase the facets land in; 4 x 166.4 = 665.6 mm2 against the 603.1 measured. So the 2.83 reading is ~1.5x facet phase on top of a real but much smaller difference: our motor metal's visible silhouette at this aspect is 2,429.7 mm2 against the CAD's 1,836.4 mm2, a ratio of 1.32, because our can and adapter are one plain 27 mm cylinder where the CAD's bell has a waist and a shroud. At 45 deg, which spans six of our facets, the ratio is measured and scored against the unchanged band.
deviations.why_not_fixed_by_geometry: Raising MOTOR_SEG would move the number without being a better model of anything: at 36 segments the facets land at +-5 deg and the 10 deg reading gets WORSE (1.49x a smooth cylinder), at 48 it is 1.12x and at 72 it is 1.00x. Choosing the tessellation that makes a row pass is what plan D.5.4 forbids, and 36 and 48 segments both break the parts library's own P3_motor budget of 600 faces per can (768 faces at 36). The real shape difference the silhouette row shows - a plain cylinder instead of the CAD's belled profile - is a revision-2 item, recorded here.
scored_instead: C.5 facing/motor metal facing az180 el0 (45 deg) ratio to CAD motor solids
kept_as_report: C.5 facing/motor metal facing az180 el0 (10 deg) ratio to CAD motor solids
C.5 facing/motor visible silhouette az180 el0, ratio to CAD motor solids
deviations.evidence_limits: A 45 deg cone is a coarser question than the plan asked. It is the narrowest cone that spans several facets of this mesh; the honest reading of the 10 deg row on a 24-gon is that it cannot be asked, not that it is 2.83.

_threshold_file_deviations_about: ⭐ 2026-09-18 b6 (independent verification). RULING 1(b)/(c) and RULING 4 require every deviation to be scored explicitly as a report-only row with its measured value printed, so that the pre-deviation pass/fail count is recoverable from any run. Six of matrice4e's ten deviations (DEV-5 ... DEV-10) already were. The other four were written INTO the frozen threshold file before the first acceptance run and nothing printed the row they replaced, so the pre-deviation count could not be recovered. They are listed here with the plan's own bound, and benchmark/mesh_rev1_acceptance_matrice4e.py now prints each one as a report row marked WOULD FAIL / WOULD PASS. No gate row, no gate verdict and no threshold value changes: the run is still 163 scored / 160 passed / 3 failed, and the frozen threshold file is still sha256 58872e31193330861cc3220277fabf91046c9aef3df5872566b1afddf0333942.
